_about.what: Verification status of each intervention in the county-bundle catalog (D.catalog). The page shows a dollar or $-per-$1 figure only for verified and partially_verified items; unverified items are listed by name only.

status.verified: effect size and cost both confirmed against a source fetched in the audit
status.partially_verified: one side confirmed (or, for items with no dollar effect, the cost cites a named public document that was not re-fetched)
status.unverified: neither confirmed, source not found, not reproducible, or labelled an unchecked AI research pass in the catalog

effect.checked: the effect size used was found in the cited source's text
effect.unchecked: the study exists or is named, but the number used was not confirmed (or the item estimates no dollar effect)
effect.misapplied: the number is real but applied outside the conditions the study measured
effect.not_found: the cited study or its data could not be found

cost.checked: the unit cost was found in a fetched document
cost.unchecked: the cost cites a document that was not re-fetched, or has no source
cost.contradicted: the cost used differs materially from the document it cites

street_trees.evidence: City Pretty local hedonic (3,386 Westside sales): no regression code or sales data in repo or git history; irreproducible. Shipped to 637 non-LA counties as "local sales estimate".
street_trees.notes: Unverified: the catalog's grade-A effect comes from a 'City Pretty local hedonic' regression (3,386 Westside sales, 2022-24) whose code and sales data are not in the repository or its git history, so it cannot be reproduced. Confirmed street-tree studies exist in research/effects.csv (Donovan & Butry 2010; Sander, Polasky & Haight 2010) but the model does not use them yet. The same 0.24% was shipped to 637 non-LA counties labelled 'local sales estimate'. Cost cites a named public document that was not re-fetched (most LA agency sites return 403 from the audit machine). | 2026-11-16 re-check: Donovan & Butry 2010 measured the bundle of existing street trees fronting a house (+3.0% of median price), not newly planted trees within 50 m, so it does not confirm the engine's 0.24% per new tree.

brt.evidence: Effect: Beaudoin & Tyndall, UHERO WP 2023-03 (re-fetched 2026-11-16, uhero.hawaii.edu/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/UHEROwp2303.pdf): "We estimate a 5-7% price premium for homes located within a 20 minute walk of a BRT station." Engine uses 5.0%. Cost: LA Metro Board file 2026-0295 (Legistar matter 12412, approved by the Board 2026-05-28): "ESTABLISHING a Life-of-Project (LOP) budget for the North Hollywood to Pasadena Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) Project in the amount of $428,988,535"; metro.net project page: 19 miles. $428,988,535 / 19 mi = $22.58M per mile; engine uses $11.3M for 0.5 mile.
brt.notes: Model choices not validated: the engine applies the effect to 1.5x the block group's homes (the study's catchment is a 20-minute walk of a station) and uses one LA project's cost per mile everywhere. Other studies in research/effects.csv find no significant effect (Benson & Cao, Twin Cities A Line) or declines for single-family homes (Acton, Le & Miller 2022: Miami -2.5%, Pittsburgh -11.4%).
brt.caution: other BRT studies find no effect or declines

affordable_housing.evidence: Diamond & McQuade abstract confirms +6.5%/-2.5% (OpenAlex). MISAPPLIED: study +6.5% is for tracts with median income under ~$26k; engine applies it below LA median $93,240
affordable_housing.notes: Diamond & McQuade's +6.5% (confirmed in their abstract) is for low-income neighborhoods; the catalog's citation gives the cut-off as median income under ~$26k (the abstract does not state the figure), and -2.5% in higher-income areas. The original build applied +6.5% wherever income was below LA's median ($93,240): misapplied. The page now shows this estimate only where the block group's median household income is below $26,000. Cost cites a named public document that was not re-fetched (most LA agency sites return 403 from the audit machine).

noise_wall.evidence: Effect: Moretti & Wheeler 6.8% within 100 m, quote re-found (effects.csv row 21). Cost: the catalog cites Metro's February 2019 soundwall report; that presentation (LA Metro Legistar file 2018-0787, attachment 'Presentation', fetched 2026-11-16) says "$10 Million/mile if placed adjacent to the freeway shoulder" and "$20 Million/mile if on bridge structures or retaining walls" (design and construction). The engine uses $2,485 per metre = $4.0M per mile, 40% of the cited shoulder figure.
noise_wall.notes: Downgraded 2026-11-16: the shipped cost understates the cited source about 2.5x, so the shipped return per $1 is overstated by the same factor. pipeline/engine.py now uses $6,214/m (the cited $10M/mile); shipped bundles keep the old figure until they are rebuilt, so no dollar figure is shown.
